finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized() (returns boolean) but ignores the result, so any authenticated user can delete any project. Unlike authorize(), which throws, authorized() never enforces anything.
finding.source: Any authenticated user supplying req.params.id of a project they do not own

trace.note: authorized() returns false for non-owner but return value is discarded
authorized() only returns a boolean, never throws

finding.guards_checked: Compared with the PUT route which correctly uses authorize() that throws 403; no middleware in this file enforces ownership; authentication of req.user is assumed from outside this file. If the project does not exist, project is undefined and authorized() throws TypeError (500), a minor robustness issue.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at api.js:18. No middleware in this file enforces ownership. The PUT route correctly uses the throwing authorize() at api.js:25.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (api.js:12-14) as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated non-owner. Authentication itself is assumed from outside this file and could not be checked.
